sidebar.pairWifiHelp: Pair an iPhone or iPad (iOS 27 or later) over the local network, without a cable
list.emptyDetail: Connect an iPhone or iPad with a cable, unlock it and trust this computer. Or pair one over Wi-Fi, without a cable.
list.noUsbmuxd.title: Install Apple Devices
list.noUsbmuxd.detail: To connect with a cable, Windows needs Apple Devices (or iTunes). Install it, open it once and accept its license, then plug the device in again.
list.noUsbmuxd.waiting: This list updates by itself once Apple Devices runs. Devices paired over Wi-Fi work without it.
device.disconnectedHelp: Disconnected. Connect the cable again and unlock the device.
device.unsupported: DeviceSteer works only with iOS 27 or later. Earlier versions don’t allow the screen sharing and remote control it needs. Update the device in Settings › General › Software Update, if its model can run iOS 27.
device.unsupportedRuns: DeviceSteer works only with iOS 27 or later, and this device runs {os}. Earlier versions don’t allow the screen sharing and remote control it needs. Update the device in Settings › General › Software Update, if its model can run iOS 27.
zoom.actualHelp: Actual size: one point per pixel (⌘0)
zoom.actualHelp@windows: Actual size: one point per pixel (Ctrl+0)
keyboard.label: Keyboard
keyboard.stateOn: Keyboard: a hardware keyboard is connected and keys go to the device while the pointer is over the screen (⌘K to stop)
keyboard.stateOn@windows: Keyboard: a hardware keyboard is connected and keys go to the device while the pointer is over the screen (Ctrl+K to stop)
keyboard.statePaused: Keyboard: paused while the agent is in control (⌘K to turn off)
keyboard.statePaused@windows: Keyboard: paused while the agent is in control (Ctrl+K to turn off)
keyboard.forwardHelp: Connects a hardware keyboard to the device, and keys go to it while the pointer is over the screen. The device’s input source decides what they type (Control-Space switches it)
keyboard.softwareHelp: Show or hide the on-screen keyboard while a hardware keyboard is connected
keyboard.softwareAlone: The on-screen keyboard shows by itself while no hardware keyboard is connected (⌘K connects one).
keyboard.softwareAlone@windows: The on-screen keyboard shows by itself while no hardware keyboard is connected (Ctrl+K connects one).
keyboard.sharedHelp: Keep the Mac and device clipboards in step while the screen is live, text only. Paused while the agent is in control; never sends what a password manager marks private
keyboard.sharedHelp@windows: Keep the PC and device clipboards in step while the screen is live, text only. Paused while the agent is in control; never sends what a password manager marks private
keyboard.sharedMacOnly: The shared clipboard works on macOS only for now
keyboard.getHelp: Put the device clipboard’s text on the Mac clipboard
keyboard.getHelp@windows: Put the device clipboard’s text on the PC clipboard
keyboard.sendHelp: Put the Mac clipboard’s text on the device clipboard, without pasting it: paste it on the device yourself
keyboard.sendHelp@windows: Put the PC clipboard’s text on the device clipboard, without pasting it: paste it on the device yourself
clipboard.agentHasDevice: The agent has the device: take over first to send the clipboard.
clipboard.sent: Copied to {device}. Paste it on the device.
clipboard.notText: The {device} clipboard holds no text (an image or other content); only text is copied.
voiceover.warning: Taps select instead of activating, so agent input won’t do what it expects.
stage.disconnected: Connect the cable again and unlock the device. If it is restarting, wait: it continues here once it is back.
stage.daemonClosed: The connection to the device closed again. Try again to reconnect.
session.blockedHint: The agent is in control. Take over to use the device.
deviceBar.label: Device
screenshot.notEncoded: the screen could not be encoded as PNG
record.label: Record
settings.locationInvalid: Enter a latitude (-90 to 90) and a longitude (-180 to 180) in degrees.
settings.unsupported: This device can’t be used with DeviceSteer.
settings.afterAvailable: Settings show once the device is available.
settings.afterSetup: Settings show once the device is set up.
settings.afterReconnect: Settings show once the device is connected again.
settings.afterPairing: Settings show once a device is paired.
info.name: Name
setup.heading: Set up this device
setup.lead: The screen can be shown once these steps are done.
setup.waitingOnDevice: Waiting for you on the device
setup.trust.title: Trust this computer
setup.trust.text: Unlock the device and press Pair. When it asks “Trust This Computer?”, tap Trust and enter the passcode.
setup.trust.noCable: Connect the device with a USB cable, or pair it over Wi-Fi without one (iOS 27 or later).
setup.trust.timeout: Nobody tapped Trust within {duration}. Unlock the device, press Try Again and tap Trust when it asks.
setup.developerMode.title: Developer Mode
setup.developerMode.text: Press Show Switch, then on the device open Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode, turn it on and tap Restart. After the restart, unlock it, tap Turn On and enter the passcode.
setup.developerMode.timeout: Developer Mode wasn’t turned on within {duration}. Press Try Again to keep waiting. If you turn it on without the app, this card notices by itself.
setup.diskImage.title: Prepare developer tools
setup.diskImage.text: Installs Apple’s developer tools on the device, downloading them once if Xcode isn’t installed. Nothing to do on the device; needed again after some restarts.
pair.heading: Pair a device over Wi-Fi
pair.lead: For an iPhone or iPad with iOS 27 or later, on the same network as this computer.
pair.step1.title: Start pairing on the device
pair.step1.text: Open Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode. Under Other Devices, tap Pair with DeviceSteer, then tap Pair.
pair.step2.title: Enter the device’s passcode
pair.step2.text: The device asks for its own passcode first.
pair.step3.title: Enter the code shown here
pair.step3.text: Then it asks for the 6-digit code shown on DeviceSteer.
pair.typeCode: Type this on the device, where it asks for the code shown on DeviceSteer. It is not the device’s passcode.
pair.shownAs: This computer shows up on the device as DeviceSteer while this card is open.
pair.noDevice: No device started pairing within {duration}. Check that it is on the same network as this computer, press Try Again, then tap Pair with DeviceSteer on the device.
pair.noCode: The code wasn’t entered on the device within {duration}. Press Try Again for a new code.
move.title: Move DeviceSteer to Applications?
move.fromDiskImage: DeviceSteer is running from its disk image.
move.fromTranslocated: DeviceSteer is running from a temporary copy macOS made of the download.
move.why: Move it to the Applications folder so coding agents can use it and it can update itself. It reopens from there.
move.replaceVersion: The Applications folder already has DeviceSteer {old}. Replace it? The old one goes to the Trash.
move.replaceVersionWithThis: The Applications folder already has DeviceSteer {old}. Replace it with this one ({version})? The old one goes to the Trash.
move.replaceOther: The Applications folder already has another copy of DeviceSteer. Replace it? The old one goes to the Trash.
move.replaceOtherWithThis: The Applications folder already has another copy of DeviceSteer. Replace it with this one ({version})? The old one goes to the Trash.
move.noPermission: DeviceSteer can’t write to the Applications folder. In Finder, drag DeviceSteer into Applications, then open it from there.
agentSheet.title: Set Up Agents
agentSheet.lead: Let coding agents on this Mac use your iPhone or iPad: DeviceSteer adds its command-line tool and its skill, linked to this app so they update with it. Change this later in Settings › Agents.
agentSheet.lead@windows: Let coding agents on this PC use your iPhone or iPad: DeviceSteer adds its command-line tool and its skill, linked to this app so they update with it. Change this later in Settings › Agents.
agents.sharedName: Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and others
agents.replaceInSettings: Replace it in Settings › Agents if you want.
agents.cliNeeded: Agents need the command-line tool to operate devices. Without it, the skills won’t work.
agents.conflictLink: A link to {target} is already there.
agents.conflictLinkElsewhere: A link to somewhere else is already there.
agents.conflictFile: A file is already there. Replacing it moves it aside.
agents.conflictFolder: A folder is already there. Replacing it moves it aside.
agents.unavailable.dev_build: Agent setup works in the installed app, not in a development build.
agents.unavailable.move_to_applications: Move DeviceSteer to the Applications folder and open it from there to set up agents.
agents.unavailable.incomplete_build: This build of the app doesn’t include the command-line tool and the skill.
prefs.title: Settings
prefs.languageNote: Some messages from the device connection and the command-line tool stay in English.
prefs.openOnSession: Open the viewer when an agent starts a session
prefs.openOnSessionNote: The viewer opens on that device, or comes forward if it is open, without taking the keyboard from the app you are typing in.
prefs.agentsLead: Coding agents on this Mac operate your devices through DeviceSteer’s command-line tool and skill. Both are links into this app, so they update with it.
prefs.agentsLead@windows: Coding agents on this PC operate your devices through DeviceSteer’s command-line tool and skill. Both are links into this app, so they update with it.
prefs.replaceHelp: Replace what is there with DeviceSteer’s link
prefs.pathShell: {dir} isn’t on your shell’s PATH. Add it to your shell profile, e.g. {line} in {file}, then open a new terminal.
prefs.pathWindows: {dir} isn’t on your PATH. Add it to your user Path (Edit environment variables for your account), then open a new terminal.
prefs.updateReady: DeviceSteer {version} is ready to download. The app restarts to finish; device daemons keep running.
error.mac_clipboard_empty: The Mac clipboard holds no text.
error.mac_clipboard_empty@windows: The PC clipboard holds no text.
